messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] HIGH: elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts in us-west-2 for /v1/generate. 12.3% 5xx over 5m, queue depth on batching-scheduler up x8. Pager triggered to #eng-oncall. Dashboard: https://grafana/redwood/d/abc123 (reacted :rotating_light:)
arjun_k: taking this — oncall here. collecting logs and tracing. who from runtime can help triage?
sara_v: I’m on it. ingesting logs now — one scheduler pod (scheduler-42) looks overloaded, queue_len climbing and batches not progressing (head-of-line blocking). KV cache hit rate dropped. sample log line: 
```json
{"ts":"2026-03-15T09:12:03Z","pod":"scheduler-42","queue_len":472,"batch_size":1,"lat_ms":12000}
```
tim_r: looks like thundering small requests causing lots of tiny batches. propose: scale scheduler replicas to 6, enable emergency backpressure to shed tiny non-critical requests, and route 10% traffic to fallback model as an immediate safety valve. I'll run infra changes.
tim_r: executing:
```
kubectl scale deploy/scheduler -n production --replicas=6
redwoodctl config set --path /services/scheduler/emergency_backpressure true
```
ops-bot: action accepted — scheduler replicas scaling 3 -> 6 (rolling) (reacted :rocket:)
jen_h: we have a stuck batch id=abc123 that is monopolizing the executor. we have an admin evict endpoint: `/admin/evict?req=...` — can we evict?
arjun_k: evicting now: `curl -X POST "https://platform.internal/admin/evict?req=abc123"` -> 200 OK.
sara_v: eviction cleared the stuck batch. queue_len dropping 472 -> 60. still seeing elevated tail latency though. starting canary routing to fallback model (gpt-small) at 10% to reduce pressure.
mike_s: applying routing change:
```
redwoodctl route set --service scheduler --fallback-model gpt-small --pct 10
```
ops-bot: routing change applied.
lia_m: customer impact: three enterprise customers (cust-phi, cust-pay, cust-bot) reported >200 errors combined in last 10m. SLOs likely affected. support & CSM notified.
arjun_k: setting incident severity SEV2. @sara_v own runtime fix, @tim_r own infra. I’ll handle comms.
sara_v: found a regression in the batching window logic introduced in last deploy — single-request batches can monopolize executor in edge-case. building hotfix to restore previous backoff behavior.
sara_v: hotfix steps:
```
git checkout hotfix/batching-window-edge
bazel build //runtime:scheduler && redwoodctl deploy --service scheduler --image redwood/scheduler:hotfix-2026-03-15
```
ops-bot: hotfix rollout started (canary to 2 nodes).
tim_r: rolling restart of affected scheduler pods completed. replicas stable at 6. emergency backpressure flag true. metrics: 5xx dropping from 12.3% -> 2.1%, timeouts decreasing.
arjun_k: handing monitoring to @sara_v for 15m post-mitigation watch. @tim_r please keep infra on 30m watch. I'll coordinate customer comms and status page.
sara_v: monitoring — queues continue to fall, tail latency trending down. will open follow-up ticket for batching-window regression and add targeted unit+integration tests to catch HOL scenarios. initial RCA: batching window edge case + high volume of tiny requests -> head-of-line queueing -> timeouts.
lia_m: support updated customers and posted interim status. will draft postmortem and coordinate SLA analysis.
arjun_k: incident mitigated at 1978823678 — hotfix deployed, scale applied, fallback routing enabled, stuck batches evicted. next steps: postmortem, add auto-evict on long-running batches, add metric alert for per-pod queue depth and HOL detection, automated load-shed for low-tier.
incident-bot: Incident marked resolved by pager at 1978823678 (reacted :white_check_mark:)
